fact: The Personal Data Protection Office, established under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, is headed by director Baker Birikujja, who addressed an ISACA Kampala breakfast on 18 August 2026.
The PDPO director says the Data Protection and Privacy Act requires registration of data collectors and processors and makes failure to register a criminal offence.

The PDPO director says 14,697 of an estimated 50,000 entities required to register have registered, and that the office has written to defaulters and taken some to court with the CID and the DPP, naming no case.
The Personal Data Protection Office, with National Personal Data Protection Director Baker Birikujja, issued a decision on 20 February 2026 under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap. 97.

The PDPO decided a complaint against WhatsApp LLC and Meta Platforms under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap. 97, and found a failure to demonstrate compliance with its cross-border transfer requirements.

The PDPO's decision of 20 February 2026 partly upheld the AdLegal International complaint and issued five corrective orders to WhatsApp LLC, with Meta joined for implementation only; no fine was imposed.
By letter of 17 July 2026 the PDPO confirmed WhatsApp LLC had implemented the corrective measures within the prescribed timelines, and no appeal was lodged in the statutory period.
The PDPO decision of 20 February 2026 and its 17 July 2026 closure letter are enforcement events under the Act within the twelve months to the report of 29 July 2026.
The case against Vuka Africa's finance manager was brought by PDPO director Baker Birikujja, and NITA-U and the PDPO launched the six-month 'Beera Ku Guard' data protection campaign.
A magistrate court heard charges under Sections 5, 35 and 36 of the Data Protection and Privacy Act, covering registration and unlawful obtaining and disclosure of personal data.

On 3 December 2025 the finance manager of Vuka Africa Ltd pleaded guilty before Grade One Magistrate Geoffrey Akena to failing to register with the PDPO and was fined five currency points (sh100,000) or two months' imprisonment.

The Beera Ku Guard campaign, run by NITA-U with the PDPO over six months to reach 70 percent of Ugandans, aims to register at least 1,000 data-controlling organisations with the PDPO by 2026; the report is dated 11 December 2025.
Acting PDPO director Baker Birikujja ruled on 18 July 2025; the report describes the PDPO as an independent office under NITA-U.
The PDPO ruled under the Data Protection and Privacy Act Cap 97, Section 19 and Regulation 30, with appeals to the Minister for ICT within 30 days.
The ruling applies Regulation 30 on cross-border transfers and Regulation 48 on offences, a fine up to three currency points a day or six months' imprisonment.

In a ruling dated 18 July 2025 on a complaint of 8 November 2024, the PDPO found Google in breach for operating unregistered and transferring data abroad without adequate safeguards, and gave it 30 days to register and submit transfer-compliance evidence; compensation was declined as outside its authority.
The decision in Complaint No. PDPO 086/2025 is signed by Baker Birikujja as National Personal Data Protection Director of the Personal Data Protection Office.
The PDPO decided the complaint under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap 97, citing its provisions on consent, minimisation and cross-border processing (Section 19).

The decision is rendered under the Data Protection and Privacy Regulations, 2021, applying Regulation 30 on adequacy, Regulation 45(2) and (3) on decisions and enforcement notices, Regulation 46 on appeal and Regulation 48 on offences.

The PDPO's decision of 20 February 2026 partly upheld a complaint against WhatsApp LLC and Meta Platforms, Inc. and ordered, within 90 days, a revised Uganda privacy policy, separation of core and ancillary processing with opt-in, a Regulation 30 adequacy assessment, an intra-group DPIA and a legitimate-interests assessment.
The decision records that the Office's 18 July 2025 decision in Ssekamwa Frank and 3 Others v Google LLC held the Act applies to foreign entities serving persons in Uganda, and applies that holding.

The Personal Data Protection Office decided complaint no. 08/11/24/6683 (Ssekamwa Frank and 3 others v Google LLC) on 18 July 2025, finding Google LLC a data controller and collector in breach of the Act's registration duty (section 29) and cross-border transfer duty (section 19), and ordering it to register and to document its transfer compliance within 30 days.
